tool_args.rationale: The branch probe established that stronger sink gradients suppress transfer, but both new measurements also changed the drive. All seven rows are endpoints at H = 0.6. The trajectory batch can test whether the response has a second time scale before committing to a static or coupled law.

considered_alternatives.option: Static saturating transfer with sink inhibition
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The seven endpoints show saturation and sink inhibition, but several static laws can explain them and predict different responses at unmeasured input–gradient combinations.
Every observation uses the same horizon and initial state, so the endpoint data cannot distinguish a delayed second stage from a static response.
The auxiliary measurement would not distinguish static transfer from coupled dynamics.
